messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected for model-serving runtime (region: us-west-2). Error class: SIGSEGV/OOM during inference. Pager escalated to on-call.
sarah: I'm on it. paging @miguel @alex for runtime debugging.
miguel: joining. any immediate customer outages reported?
carol: two customers showing ~18% error rate on generation endpoints, some timeouts. dashboard: https://console/reports/serve/us-west-2 spike around 09:12 UTC.
alex: I see a cluster-level pattern: multiple pods restarting. `kubectl get pods -n inference --selector=app=model-runner` shows CrashLoopBackOff across nodes a,b,c.
jin: past incidents like this were KV cache blowup when a particular prompt pattern triggered long prefix growth. pulling recent logs.
noah: I've put a rapid mitigation: traffic steering to fallback-v2 model (lower memory profile) for affected routes via routing service. Should reduce pressure. :arrow_right_hook:
ops-bot: Routing update executed: 42% of traffic rerouted to fallback-v2 for routes /v1/generate and /v1/chat.
alex: grabbing logs from one of the failing pods:
```
[2026-03-15T09:11:57Z] runtime: panic: segfault
#0 0x7f2b1c2a9 in attention_kernel()
#1 0x7f2b1c5d4 in run_inference_loop()
#2 0x558a4b3 in start_worker()
signal: segmentation fault (core dumped)
```
miguel: can you get `dmesg` from the node? suspect OOM killer or kernel crash.
ken: dmesg shows repeated OOM killer logs targeting `model-runner` processes, plus some vmalloc warnings. pastebin: https://paste.redwood/dmesg-569876
sarah: are these pods using quantized kernels? last deploy changed a kernel selection matrix two deploys ago.
alex: yes, new quant kernels were rolled two days ago (rollout id r-20260313). I'll roll that back on a small canary.
jin: I'm seeing memory growth traces in the runner logs before the crash: KV cache size keeps incrementing per request for some prompt IDs. suspect a leak in prefix eviction path.
noah: temporary mitigation: enforce `--kv-cache-max-entries=200` via env override on failing pods. can someone patch the daemonset config and restart one node?
emma: I'll patch the daemonset and do a rolling restart on node-a only. doing `kubectl rollout restart daemonset/model-runner -n inference --field-selector spec.nodeName=node-a` now.
carol: customer impact update: Customer A (prod) seeing 15% failed requests, region-us-west; Customer B (staging) ~22%. Support notified with workaround: route to hosted fallback model.
alex: after patch on node-a the pod on node-a stayed up for 8m but then failed again. logs show a different error this time: mmap failure while allocating 350MB for attention scratch.
```
E [2026-03-15T09:24:03Z] allocation failure: failed to mmap 367001600 bytes: Cannot allocate memory
```
miguel: that suggests fragmented memory or kernel-level limits. can we check cgroup limits and memcg stats?
ken: `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/kubepods/pod*/memory.stat` shows memory.high not set for these pods, they can grow until OOM.
sarah: set memory.high on problematic QoS class to throttle before OOM. We can apply a temporary ResourceQuota with memory limits per pod class.
noah: I'll spin up extra capacity (2x) in us-west-2 dedicated pool and mark the older host types unschedulable to force new pods onto larger instances.
ops-bot: Scaling event triggered: +4 gpus added to dedicated-us-west-2-pool-3; expected available in ~4m.
alex: still getting segfaults on older nodes after restart, but new nodes have fewer failures. correlation with host kernel versions: older nodes run kernel 5.10.x, new ones 5.15.x.
jin: possible that a driver/kernel combination causes allocator corruption with our quantized kernels. recommend immediate rollback of quant kernel picks for 5.10 nodes.
emma: started a targeted daemonset patch to disable quant kernels for nodes with kernel<5.15. Applying label and restart on two nodes now.
carol: sending customer-facing note: "We are investigating elevated error rates in us-west-2 affecting some generation requests. Traffic is partially routed to a fallback model while we mitigate. We'll update in 30 minutes." sent.
sarah: parallel work: capture core from a crashing pod for offline analysis. use `gcore` on the PID and upload to s3: `gcore -o /tmp/core.$PID $PID && aws s3 cp /tmp/core.$PID s3://redwood-cores/569876`.
alex: core collected from node-a, copied. attaching short backtrace from gdb:
```
(gdb) bt
#0  0x00007f2b1c2a9 in attention_kernel + 89
#1  0x00007f2b1c5d4 in run_inference_loop + 132
#2  0x0000558a4b33 in main_worker + 57
```
jin: analysis note: repeated pattern where `attention_kernel` mallocs, fails to handle mmap failure and later free path corrupts. could be a race in custom allocator with hugepages.
miguel: I'm pairing with infra to reproduce with stress test workload hitting long prefixes and concurrent requests. prepping harness.
noah: for immediate customer relief, increased fallback routing to 70% for affected routes and enabled per-customer rate limiting to keep requests below the leaking path threshold.
carol: that reduced customer errors to ~3% for Customer A and ~5% for Customer B. support updated.
ken: kernel team suggests backporting a driver fix to 5.10 nodes or cordoning them. cordoning option selected for now for two oldest hosts.
emma: nodes cordoned and draining completed for node-b and node-c. pods rescheduled to larger nodes.
ops-bot: incident timeline note: mitigation steps applied: routing fallback, kv cache cap, increased capacity, cordon old nodes, disabled quant kernels on old kernels.
sarah: next: schedule a postmortem, list of action items: 1) reproduce leak locally, 2) add eviction threshold (`memory.high`) for model-runner pods, 3) improve kernel/driver matrix in rollout gating, 4) add health-check that detects mmap failures and triggers graceful fallback.
alex: I'll open a PR for the eviction threshold and rollback quant kernels toggle. jin will lead the leak investigation.
jin: copying core and logs to the crash-analysis board. starting a focused debug session now. will update in 2 hours or sooner.
noah: thanks everyone. I'll keep routing at current levels until further notice. great work moving fast here. :clap:
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Severity reduced from P1 -> P2. Monitoring for regression enabled. Postmortem requested: https://boards.redwood/incidents/5698765432
